paper_title: DARWIN: towards the ultimate dark matter detector
notes: DARWIN projection paper. Constrains axion-electron coupling g_Ae via axio-electric effect for solar axions and galactic ALPs (Figure 4). Only XENON100 reference values quoted in text (g_ALP_Ae >~2e-12, g_solar_Ae >7.7e-12); DARWIN projections are described qualitatively ('almost two orders of magnitude' improvement for galactic ALPs, ~one order for solar axions) but no explicit numerical DARWIN limit values are given in the text, only shown in plots. Cannot extract reliable numerical data points. Local DM density rho0=0.3 GeV/cm^3 assumed for galactic ALP search. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 right panel: DARWIN sensitivity (blue dashed) to galactic ALPs in g_ae vs m_A. X-axis is m_A in keV/c^2 (1-40), converted to eV (1000-40000 eV). Y-axis is g_ae (axion-electron coupling), dimensionless, ranging 1e-14 to 1e-9. The DARWIN curve is the lowest (most sensitive) projection.
